display.purpose: The home greeting, one per page; 2rem at 640px and below.

headline.purpose: Lab heading and empty-state titles; 1.375rem on narrow screens.

title.purpose: Run panel and briefing titles; the wordmark at 1rem.

body-prose.purpose: Agent sentences, draft note, About, markdown preview at a 60ch measure.

body-sm.purpose: Buttons, nav links, field labels, secondary copy.

label.purpose: Stage labels, chips, date-group titles, sentence case.

mono.purpose: File names, task activity, attempt counts, time and cost figures, with tabular figures.

mono-2xs.purpose: Stage details ("2 tasks", "0/2") and kbd hints.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Rest: the composer, the new-lab button, the selected segment of a segmented control or theme switch.

shadows.name: shadow-3
shadows.purpose: Overlay: the open drawer and the toast only.

shadows.name: working-edge
shadows.purpose: State, not depth: the top edge of a run panel while it works.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Quart out: every arrival and hover.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: State flips, theme cross-fade, shimmer sweeps.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Hover, press, chip and colour changes.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: List rows, entries, disclosures, toasts, theme flip.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Page arrival, stage strike, connector fill, result rise, sidebar slide.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Arrival translate; half for soft enters; 0 under reduced motion.

motion.name: stagger
motion.purpose: Sidebar list stagger, index clamped at twelve rows; 0 under reduced motion.

motion.name: tick-draw
motion.purpose: Ticks that draw themselves; 70ms per stage, 45ms per task (capped at 8).

motion.name: arc-spin
motion.purpose: The running arc, the only mark that moves; stopped under reduced motion.

motion.name: celebration
motion.purpose: Once, only for a finish watched live; removed under reduced motion; never on a lab read from disk.

breakpoints.name: drawer
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer with scrim and top bar.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: display 2rem, panels pad 16px, run head stacks, artifact actions wrap.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: the stage rail tightens further.

breakpoints.name: coarse-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: Controls grow to 44px; row actions always visible on hover: none.

components.css: .ds-chips { display: flex; gap: 6px; } .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; height: 30px; padding: 0 12px 0 10px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--line-control, #7a6e75); background: transparent; color: var(--ink-2, #c7bdbb); font-family: var(--font-text); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 520; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1), border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1), color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-chip::before { content: ''; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1.5px solid currentColor; opacity: 0.7; } .ds-chip:hover { background: var(--surface-2, #2a2429); color: var(--ink, #f4eeea); } .ds-chip[aria-pressed='true'] { background: var(--accent-soft, rgb(255 106 77 / 0.13)); border-color: var(--accent, #ff6a4d); color: var(--accent-ink, #ff7d61); } .ds-chip[aria-pressed='true']::before { background: currentColor; opacity: 1; } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus, #ff8a70); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Marks
components.description: The state vocabulary: pending, running, waiting, done, partial, failed, lost.
components.css: .ds-marks { display: flex; gap: 14px; } .ds-mark { width: 20px; height: 20px; overflow: visible; fill: none; stroke-width: 1.6; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-mark .g { stroke: var(--ink-ghost, #877b82); } .ds-mark .arc { stroke: var(--accent-mark, #ff6a4d); stroke-width: 1.9; stroke-dasharray: 30 100; transform-origin: 8px 8px; animation: ds-spin 900ms linear infinite; } .ds-mark .a { stroke: var(--accent-mark, #ff6a4d); } .ds-mark .dot { fill: var(--accent-mark, #ff6a4d); stroke: none; } .ds-mark .d { stroke: var(--ink-3, #aa9f9e); } .ds-mark .t { stroke: var(--ink, #f4eeea); stroke-width: 1.9; } .ds-mark .t[pathLength] { stroke-dasharray: 100; animation: ds-draw 460ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1) both; } .ds-mark .notch { fill: var(--danger, #f27092); stroke: var(--bg-raised, #1a161a); stroke-width: 1.5; } .ds-mark .r, .ds-mark .x { stroke: var(--danger, #f27092); } .ds-mark .s { stroke: var(--ink-3, #aa9f9e); } @keyframes ds-spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } } @keyframes ds-draw { from { stroke-dashoffset: 100; } to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-mark .arc { animation: none; } .ds-mark .t[pathLength] { animation: none; stroke-dasharray: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Every lab is a pipeline you can watch. The system borrows its grammar from CI pipelines and IDE run panels rather than from chat wrappers: five stages present as ghosts from the first frame, each struck forward when it goes live, each drawing its own tick when it completes, and the run folding into its result in place with every earlier step still legible. Progress is real state drawn as marks, never a spinner and a paragraph.

The world is a warm-tinted near-black in stepped surfaces, built for a student alone at a laptop after midnight with the lights off, with a light theme that is a full twin rather than a filter. Neutrals lean a few degrees toward the coral so every grey reads as one warm family. Electric coral is the only accent and is spent on edges, the active mark, and the single action that moves the lab forward. Rose, a different hue, carries failure and always travels with a mark. Density is product-UI calm: a 46rem working column, a 268px labs sidebar, content as the hero.

Refused, as confirmed by the user: the generic SaaS dashboard look, purple-blue gradients, cards inside cards, heavy glassmorphism, bounce easing, emoji overload.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black ground in five stepped layers; light theme re-picked role by role.
One accent, electric coral, on edges, the active mark and one primary action per view.
Every state is a drawn mark (ring, arc, dot, tick, notch, cross, strike), never colour alone.
Bricolage Grotesque for titles, Geist for reading, Geist Mono for files, figures and machine output.
One quart-out curve family, short rises, ticks that draw themselves, one celebration.
Flat panels divided by hairlines; shadow only where something floats.

rules.name: The Edge-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: Coral lives on edges, the active mark and the one primary action in a view. A panel is never filled coral; a working run shows coral as a 1px inset top line and nowhere else.

rules.name: The One Go Rule
rules.body: A view carries at most one coral-filled action: the thing that moves the lab forward. Every other action is secondary (control-line outline on surface-2) or quiet.

rules.name: The Twin Rule
rules.body: Light is not dark inverted. Every role is re-picked for its ground; coral splits into fill, mark and ink so each clears its own contrast bar in both themes (WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 text, 3:1 marks, controls and focus).

rules.name: The Control Line Rule
rules.body: A control's boundary is line-control, always. line-strong is decoration; a control drawn with it fails 3:1.

rules.name: The Titles-Only Display Rule
rules.body: Bricolage sets titles and the wordmark, nothing else. When a briefing collapses to its done state, its title drops back to Geist.

rules.name: The Machine-Speaks-Mono Rule
rules.body: If a program, the file system or a counter produced it, it is set in Geist Mono with tabular figures, so numbers that change in place never jitter.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case at normal tracking. No uppercase tracked labels anywhere in the system.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Run panels, briefings, notices and previews are flat, bordered by a hairline. A shadow on a panel means it floats; nothing in the column floats.

rules.name: The Well-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: Inside a panel, structure is rows and hairlines. The only nested box is an inset well one step darker (preview, fail detail, input) on bg, never a raised card inside a card.

dos: Do read every colour, size, radius and duration from tokens.css; the tokens are the single source of truth for both themes.
Do give every state a mark from the Status Mark vocabulary, paired with its word.
Do keep one coral-filled action per view and draw every other boundary with line-control.
Do use coral mark for strokes and coral ink for text, never the fill coral, so each clears contrast in light mode.
Do move with the one curve family: quart-out arrivals at 160, 240 or 380ms, rises of 8px, list staggers of 30ms capped at twelve rows, transform and opacity plus stroke-dashoffset for ticks.
Do keep short fades under reduced motion while removing rises, staggers, spins and shimmers; spinners stop on a legible arc.
Do reserve the coral-spark celebration for a finish the student watched live; a lab read back from disk replays nothing.
Do set files, figures and machine output in Geist Mono with tabular figures.
donts: Don't fill panels, text or backgrounds with gradients, and never purple-blue; the only gradients are motion sweeps (skeleton shimmer, stage connector shimmer) running transparent to a token and back.
Don't put a card inside a card; nest only an inset well on bg.
Don't use bounce, overshoot or elastic easing.
Don't use heavy glassmorphism or backdrop blur.
Don't carry state by colour alone; rose never appears without a mark or words.
Don't add format chips, keyboard hints or example prompts to the home composer; formats are requested in words.
Don't set uppercase tracked labels or eyebrow text above titles.
Don't use emoji or text glyphs as icons; icons are inline SVG.
